title: Resilience Chaos Inference Workshop Lab Plan
body:
Workshop purpose and high-level narrative:
- Purpose: Run a guided, hands-on lab with a customer engineering team to validate a Redwood Inference deployment’s resilience during realistic cutover and failure modes. Focus on fallback policies, routing, and observability during model and region failures.
- Narrative: We’ll simulate controlled failures (region outage, model regression, sudden traffic surge) and walk the customer through detection, automated fallback, and post-incident triage to measure RTO/RPO and confidence in rollout policies.

Goals (measurable):
1) Confirm automated routing and model-variant fallback completes within SLOs (target: 95th percentile tail latency < 250ms increase above baseline and successful response fallback within 10s).
2) Validate alerting and dashboarding for key signals (error rate, fallbacks, model quality regressions).
3) Capture operations playbook and decision tree for production cutover to Dedicated or Private.
4) Produce an action list with owners for any gaps discovered.

Audience and roles:
- Customer engineering lead (primary decision maker)
- Customer SRE/infra (owns monitoring and on-call)
- Solutions Engineering facilitator (Aisha) - leads exercises and timekeeping
- Runtime engineer (Marco) - config & failure injection support
- Observability engineer (Evan) - dashboarding and signal interpretation
- Note taker (Sofia) - artifacts and follow-ups

Prerequisites (pre-work for customer, complete 72h before workshop):
- Provide test workload script (1k qps synthetic traffic pattern) or permission to run Redwood-provided generator against their sandbox.
- Shared access to deployment (read-only tokens) + permissions for temporary failover toggles.
- List of production-critical routes and their SLOs.
- Baseline metrics export: 48h latency, error-rate, throughput.

Logistics: 3.5 hour session (onsite or remote). Required tools: Zoom (recording), shared Slack channel, Grafana/Redwood Console access, runbook doc template.

Agenda (times in minutes):
- 00-10m: Welcome, goals, success criteria, safety rules for chaos testing
- 10-25m: Architecture walk — deployed topology, model variants, routing policies
- 25-40m: Baseline run — synthetic load to capture reference metrics (live dashboard)
- 40-60m: Exercise 1: Model regression (introduce a degraded model variant)
  - Objective: Verify automatic variant fallback and quality gating
  - Steps: flip model weights to older variant via rollout API; monitor eval key metrics and rollback triggers
- 60-80m: Debrief 1 — observations, alerts triggered, missed signals
- 80-100m: Exercise 2: Region latency spike and partial outage
  - Objective: Validate smart routing to alternate region and explain cost/latency tradeoffs
  - Steps: throttle egress to primary region; monitor traffic shift, latency, and cost estimator
- 100-115m: Short break / capture notes
- 115-150m: Exercise 3: Traffic surge + scale limits (dedicated capacity stress)
  - Objective: Observe autoscale behavior, queueing/batching effects, and graceful degradation
  - Steps: ramp to 2x expected peak; trigger burst limits; observe fallback to lower-cost model or queue-based backpressure
- 150-165m: Post-event triage — run RCA template, determine action items
- 165-210m: Synthesis: update runbook, assign owners, next steps, and close

Slide outline (for a short 12-slide deck to accompany session):
1. Title / Objectives / Safety rules (brief)
2. High-level topology diagram (hosted/dedicated/private variants)
3. Key SLOs and what we’ll measure
4. Baseline metrics snapshot (before any failures)
5. Exercise 1: model regression — hypothesis, steps, expected behavior
6. Live results: model regression (screenshots/metrics)
7. Exercise 2: region outage — hypothesis, steps, expected behavior
8. Live results: region outage (traffic routing, latency curves)
9. Exercise 3: traffic surge — hypothesis, steps, expected behavior
10. Live results: surge (autoscale events, token cost delta)
11. Final triage / decision tree (who does what when)
12. Recommended next milestones & post-workshop deliverables

Facilitation notes and prompts (what facilitator should say / ask):
- Before each exercise: "What do you expect to see in the dashboard? If that doesn’t happen, what would you do next?"
- During failure: call out thresholds we care about (error-rate > 1%, tail-latency > 2x baseline, fallback count > 0)
- Encourage real-time ownership: ask the customer SRE to mark incidents and record timestamps — these will be used to compute RTO in the debrief.
- If automated fallback doesn’t trigger: step through the policy config with the customer (policy precedence, model compatibility table, and routing weights).

Failure injection recipes (safely reversible):
1) Model regression flip: update rollout policy to 20% of traffic to known-bad variant, wait 60s, then escalate to 100% or rollback.
2) Region throttle: use egress iptables throttle or Redwood region loss simulator to add 250ms latency and 5% packet loss to primary region.
3) Surge generator: client-side load tool configurable to ramp qps using Poisson distribution; cap should be 2x normal with 1 minute plateau.

Observability: signals to watch and when to escalate:
- Latency: p50/p95/p99 for token generation and full response
- Error rate by route and model variant
- Fallback count and fallback latency delta
- Model-quality regression metric (BLEU/ROUGE/embedding-similarity on indicator prompts)
- GPU utilization, queue length, and batch sizes

Decision tree / playbook checkpoints (condensed):
- If model-quality checks fail AND fallback count < expected -> force rollback and open incident
- If region latency > threshold AND traffic not routing away -> adjust routing policy and monitor cost delta
- If autoscale fails to meet traffic -> enable burst capacity or degrade to cached responses and enable rate limiting

Artifacts to produce during session (capture and attach):
- Timeline with timestamps and screenshots for each exercise
- RCA stub filled in for each injected failure
- Updated runbook with contact list, escalation steps, and rollback play
- Action item list with owners and target dates

Success criteria for the POC (what we will hand off):
- Working runbook covering the three failure modes and verified toggles
- Dashboard with the key SLOs and pre-configured alerts (thresholds agreed with customer)
- List of configuration changes recommended for production cutover and expected impact (latency/cost estimates)
- Signed acceptance by customer SRE that the automated fallback behavior meets agreed thresholds or a prioritized gap list to close

Follow-up (owner assignments - example):
- Dashboard and alerts: Evan Ross (due in 5 working days)
- Update rollout policy to include explicit compatibility matrix: Marco Chen (due in 7 days)
- Draft final runbook and triage template: Aisha Patel & Customer SRE (due in 3 days)

Pre-session quick checklist for facilitator: 
- Confirm customer has sandbox credentials and test traffic permission
- Prepare recording + permission to capture artifacts
- Validate GitHub artifacts and make a mutable copy of runbook template
- Pre-seed dashboards with baseline 24h metrics for quicker comparison

Notes and known risks: 
- Do not run injection against customer prod without explicit sign-off; keep all tests confined to staging or dedicated sandbox.
- Some customers may not have a compatible variant for graceful fallback; identify this in pre-work.

Appendix: Quick templates (to copy into artifacts)
- RCA stub header: incident id, start/end, summary, root cause, action items, owners, verification steps
- Runbook rollback snippet: api call example to set model routing weights, CLI snippet for region drain, alert thresholds to toggle

End of document.
